To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel adaptive gradient method that cannot diverge on a problem instance known to cause Adam and other popular methods to diverge, and we show that this method performs well on a variety of machine learning tasks.

1) a new method called Expectigrag is proposed, which is a stochastic gradient descent method with adaptive stepsizes; 2) Expectigrad is proved to be robust to divergence on a convex optimization problem that causes Adam to diverge; 3) a regret bound for Expectigrad is established, showing that it is less susceptible to variance than existing methods; 4) experiments show that Expectigrad performs favorably to existing methods on high-dimensional machine learning problems.

(a) Expectigrad cannot be made to diverge by any choice of hyperparameters on the problem that causes Adam to diverge; and (b) Expectigrad is competitive with state-of-the-art adaptive stochastic optimization methods on high-dimensional tasks
